name: S75MA
description:
High end military steel. Used in high end weapons, augs, machines and so on.

Hardness: Edge-phase 68–70 HRC equivalent, bulk spine ~64–66 HRC for impact safety.

Edge retention: Outperforms legacy “super steels” by a full class; where they dull, MITHRIL-ADAMANTITE™ is still in working edge territory.

Toughness: Mithril-stabilized lattice gives tool-steel-level toughness despite the hardness, staying in the same use class as high-end cold work steels designed for abusive cutting.

Corrosion behavior: Functionally near-stainless in urban atmospheres and body fluids; maintenance is measured in months of field use, not days, better than corrosion-resistant vanadium steels.

Cutting behavior: The adamantite-enriched edge forms ultra-hard nano-carbides, so the blade bites into other metals the way old steels bit into cardboard; it keeps a “working sharp” edge through thousands of abrasive cuts where normal steels are dead.

Edge stability: At sane edge angles, it resists rolling and denting under lateral loads better than conventional ultra-hard steels, so you get both thin, aggressive geometry and survivable impact performance.

Field maintenance: Conventional abrasives skate; you need diamond or factory nano-hone rigs, like existing high-vanadium steels but worse—users trade easy sharpening for almost never needing to sharpen at all.
